facts.fact_text: The United Civil Aviation Trade Union is a trade union registered in Budapest.
Mr A. Csorba is the President of the United Civil Aviation Trade Union.

On 12 October 2012, Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) applied to the Budapest police department for authorisation to hold a demonstration on the road leading to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport.

One of the declared objectives of the demonstration was to draw the public's attention to the precarious financial situation in which the employees of Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport would find themselves if salary cuts envisaged by the company managing the airport were carried out.
The demonstration was scheduled to be held between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m. on 17 October 2012.
Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) specified that it was expected that about fifty to 100 persons would participate in the demonstration.
Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) specified that it was intended that speeches would be given at the demonstration.
Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) specified that it was intended that an open letter would be read out at the demonstration.
On 14 October 2012, the Monor police department forbade the demonstration planned for 17 October 2012 on the road leading to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport.
On 14 October 2012, the Monor police department forbade the demonstration planned for 17 October 2012 on the road leading to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport.

Section 8(1) of Act no. III of 1989 on the Right to Assembly provides that if the holding of an event subject to prior notification seriously endangers the proper functioning of the representative bodies or courts, or results in a disproportionate hindrance of the circulation of traffic, the police may ban the holding of the event at the place or time indicated in the notification, within 48 hours from the receipt of the notification by the authority.
The Monor police department was of the view that the planned demonstration would endanger traffic.
The Monor police department was of the view that the planned demonstration would render Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport inaccessible, infringing passengers' right to leave the country.

The Monor police department was of the view that the demonstration would breach the traffic code, since those parts of the road not used for traffic were not supposed to be accessed by pedestrians or be used for parking.

The applicants argued that a demonstration could only be forbidden on the grounds of a need to ensure traffic safety if there were no alternative means of access to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport.
The applicants argued that the demonstration would not constitute any greater hindrance to traffic than would roadworks.
The Budapest Surroundings High Court (Budapest Környéki Törvényszék) endorsed in essence the Monor police department's reasoning for forbidding the demonstration.
